{"consolidated_memory":"CACHE MISS STORM INCIDENTS IN build/bazel/BUILD.bazel

THREE SEPARATE OCCASIONS with distinct root causes, triggers, and fixes:

OCCASION 1: [2026-02-11]
- File: build/bazel/BUILD.bazel
- Problem: Cache miss storm in the build graph
- Trigger: Only affected users in negative UTC offset timezones
- Signal: Rebuild of targets that should have been cached
- Root cause: Serialiser dropping fields it did not know
- Fix: Switched to strict schema that rejects unknown fields
- PR #2293 on branch fix/cache-miss-storm-1
- Reproduction: Build twice with no source change
- Result: Nightly rollup matched source counts for 28 days running

OCCASION 2: [2026-05-07]
- File: build/bazel/BUILD.bazel
- Problem: Cache miss storm in the build graph
- Trigger: When two requests raced on the same key
- Signal: Rebuild of targets that should have been cached
- Root cause: Two writes never wrapped in a transaction
- Fix: Wrapped both writes in one transaction
- PR #6485 on branch fix/cache-miss-storm-2
- Reproduction: Build twice with no source change
- Result: Backlog cleared 19 minutes after deploy
- Stack: Starlark
- Covering check: Remote cache hit rate check in CI

OCCASION 3: [2026-08-24]
- File: build/bazel/BUILD.bazel
- Problem: Cache miss storm in the build graph
- Trigger: Only for payloads above roughly two megabytes
- Signal: Rebuild of targets that should have been cached
- Root cause: Listener registered but never removed
- Fix: Removed listener on teardown and asserted it in test
- PR #8626 on branch fix/cache-miss-storm-3
- Reproduction: Build twice with no source change
- Result: Flaky test went from 76 failures per hundred runs to zero

PATTERN: All three incidents shared the same corner of build/bazel/BUILD.bazel, allowing context to carry over across fixes. Common reproduction method across all three: building twice with no source change reliably surfaced each variant."}
